eden: quick report — converted the nextjs-sample to a custom bundler pipeline (rollup + esbuild) to match a partner. Everything seems fine locally, but on edge (Cloudflare Pages / Netlify Edge) our SDK retry path ends up concatenating Authorization headers across retries. Node server and local SSR behave fine.

harper: ouch. build or runtime?

eden: runtime. initial request 401 as expected, retry shows header doubled (comma separated). logs: 
```
[redwood] auth: 401 Unauthorized
Request headers: Authorization: Bearer BAD_KEY
Retrying...
Request headers: Authorization: Bearer BAD_KEY, Authorization: Bearer BAD_KEY
```

mike: that pattern usually means a Headers instance was reused when constructing a retry Request. Which import style and package entry are you using?

eden: named ESM import: `import { create } from '@redwood/inference'`. If I change to `const { create } = require('@redwood/inference/dist/cjs')` the issue disappears.

harper: interesting — so packaging/exports map might be involved. Also bundlers sometimes inline polyfills for fetch/Headers and those implementations can behave differently when cloning or when passed into Request constructors.

mike: can you paste the tiny handler and repro steps?

eden: sure: 
1) git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sample-apps -b edge-bundler-parity-repro
2) cd custom-rollup-edge
3) npm ci
4) REDWOOD_API_KEY=invalid npm run build:edge && npm run preview:edge
5) curl -v http://localhost:8787/api/complete

handler: 
```ts
// src/api/complete.ts
import { create } from '@redwood/inference';
const client = create({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY });
export async function post() {
  const r = await client.generate({ prompt: 'hi' });
  return new Response(await r.text());
}
```

harper: thanks. quick local workaround?

eden: I patched retry code to explicitly clone headers: 
```js
const safeHeaders = new Headers(origReq.headers || {});
safeHeaders.set('Authorization', `Bearer ${apiKey}`);
const retryReq = new Request(origReq, { headers: safeHeaders });
```
That fixes the duplication under miniflare and on Netlify dev.

mike: good defensive change. We should avoid relying on Request cloning semantics across runtimes. Also, any TS/typing issues while you were swapping imports?

eden: yes — separate but related. VSCode/tsserver fails to resolve overloads for create() when importing the ESM entry in the rollup-built project. IntelliSense works when pointing at dist/cjs. Running `tsc --noEmit` against a minimal repro project errors: 
```
TS7016: Could not find a declaration file for module '@redwood/inference'.
// or overloads for create() not found
```

harper: that's a packaging bug — package.json exports likely don't point to `.d.ts` for the ESM subpath. We should ensure the exports map has a `types` entry for both the import and require subpaths. Example recommended exports snippet: 
```json
"exports": {
  "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
  "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js",
  "types": "./dist/types/index.d.ts"
}
```
(not exact shape — ensure tsc + node resolution both work).

mike: actionables please.

eden: proposed plan: 
- Push minimal repro branch with the rollup config, netlify/vercel preview commands, and a tiny README (I can do that today).
- Open PR to make the retry path always construct a fresh Headers object (and add a unit test that simulates an edge fetch clone) — mike will take that.
- Add a CI matrix job that builds sample-apps with rollup/vite/webpack + minify options and runs the bundle under worker shims (miniflare/cloudflare preview) to catch bundler-induced differences — harper will add this.
- Patch package.json exports to include explicit types for the ESM entry and add a small `tsc --noEmit` check in CI against a fresh ESM consumer project — eden will open this PR.

ci-bot: queued job: devex/edge-bundler-parity-repro (#889) - matrix: cloudflare/workers-v8, netlify-v8, wrangler-miniflare.

sara: small note from support — a few users have hit this and worked around it by importing CJS directly; we should prioritize a fix to avoid churn.

mike: agreed. defensive cloning + typings fix + CI should cover it. I'll add tests for the retry logic and an integration that runs the built bundles under our worker runner.

eden: extra weirdness: switching to default import (`import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'`) occasionally prevents the duplication. That hints at our ESM->CJS interop wrapper or bundler transforms changing closure scope. I've logged that in the repro README and linked sdk#472.

harper: thanks — once CI finishes we can cut a patch release if the tests pass. Keep this thread updated with PR links. :rocket:
